report_name: Blind Eagle APT Uses HTML Smuggling to Target Latin American Entities

threat_actors.name: Blind Eagle
threat_actors.description: A Spanish-speaking APT group, believed to be of South American origin, conducting an espionage and financially motivated campaign against entities in Latin America. The group uses spear-phishing with judicial themes and HTML smuggling to deliver a custom RAT.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: Victims receive a phishing email impersonating an official body, containing a link that initiates the HTML smuggling attack chain.

attack_patterns.name: HTML Smuggling
attack_patterns.description: The group uses JavaScript embedded in a webpage (delivered via link or SVG file) to dynamically construct and download a malicious ZIP archive on the victim's machine, bypassing network security scanners.

attack_patterns.name: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: A malicious JavaScript file within the smuggled ZIP archive is executed by the user to act as a dropper for the final payload.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: The dropper script employs techniques to bypass the Windows Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) and Event Tracing for Windows (ETW), blinding security products from its malicious actions.

attack_patterns.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: The dropper script establishes persistence by placing a file in the Windows Startup folder.

attack_patterns.name: Keylogging
attack_patterns.description: The custom RAT used by Blind Eagle is capable of logging victim keystrokes to steal information.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The custom RAT exfiltrates stolen data, such as logged keystrokes, to an attacker-controlled server.

malware.name: Blind Eagle RAT
malware.description: A custom Remote Access Trojan (RAT) deployed as the final payload. It is derived from AsyncRAT and DCRat and is capable of data exfiltration and keystroke logging.

malware.name: AsyncRAT
malware.description: A commodity RAT that served as a code base for the custom RAT used by Blind Eagle.

malware.name: DCRat
malware.description: A commodity RAT that served as a code base for the custom RAT used by Blind Eagle.

identities.name: Government entities in Latin America
identities.description: Government organizations in Latin America targeted by Blind Eagle's espionage campaign.

identities.name: Judicial entities in Latin America
identities.description: Judicial organizations in Latin America targeted by Blind Eagle's espionage campaign.

identities.name: Financial entities in Latin America
identities.description: Financial organizations in Latin America targeted by Blind Eagle's espionage and financially motivated campaign.

identities.name: Educational organizations in Latin America
identities.description: Educational organizations in Latin America targeted by Blind Eagle's espionage campaign.

identities.name: Office of the Attorney General of Colombia
identities.description: The official branding of this Colombian government body was impersonated in phishing emails to lend legitimacy to the lures.

indicators.name: HTML Smuggling File Download via Blob URL
indicators.pattern:
title: HTML Smuggling File Download via Blob URL
id: 3a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Detects file downloads originating from a 'blob:' URL, which is a strong indicator of HTML smuggling techniques used by groups like Blind Eagle.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/blind-eagle-threat-group-launches-new-phishing-campaign-in-latin-america
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-11
tags:
  - attack.t1027.006
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|startswith: 'blob:http'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects file downloads originating from a 'blob:' URL, which is a strong indicator of HTML smuggling techniques.

indicators.name: Suspicious Wscript/Cscript Execution from Browser
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Wscript/Cscript Execution from Browser
id: 4b2c3d4e-5f6a-4891-8cde-f12345678901
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of Windows Script Host (wscript.exe or cscript.exe) with a parent process of a common web browser, a TTP used by Blind Eagle after HTML smuggling.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/blind-eagle-threat-group-launches-new-phishing-campaign-in-latin-america
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-11
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\chrome.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\iexplore.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects the execution of Windows Script Host (wscript.exe or cscript.exe) with a parent process of a common web browser, a TTP used by Blind Eagle after HTML smuggling.

indicators.name: PowerShell Execution with Encoded Command
indicators.pattern:
title: PowerShell Execution with Encoded Command
id: 5c3d4e5f-6a7b-4012-8def-123456789012
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of 'powershell -EncodedCommand', which can be used by droppers, like those from Blind Eagle, to execute obfuscated commands and bypass AMSI.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/blind-eagle-threat-group-launches-new-phishing-campaign-in-latin-america
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-11
tags:
  - attack.t1027.010
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -EncodedCommand '
      - ' -enc '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of 'powershell -EncodedCommand', which can be used by droppers to execute obfuscated commands and bypass AMSI.

indicators.name: Persistence via Startup Folder File Creation
indicators.pattern:
title: Persistence via Startup Folder File Creation
id: 6d4e5f6a-7b8c-4123-8ef0-234567890123
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of new files in the user's Startup folder, a common persistence technique used by malware like the Blind Eagle RAT.
references:
  - https://www.scworld.com/brief/blind-eagle-threat-group-launches-new-phishing-campaign-in-latin-america
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-11
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.persistence
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
indicators.description: Detects the creation of new files in the user's Startup folder, a common persistence technique.
